title: Chinese Open-Weight Models Closing In, Anthropic Warns
source_used: The Decoder (same story; BankInfoSecurity page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says Zhipu AI's open-weight GLM-5.3 can build complete cyber exploits on its own, like Claude Mythos Preview, but shipped without effective safeguards.

On a benchmark of Chrome V8 bugs GLM-5.3 built a working exploit in 50 of 410 attempts versus 56 for Mythos Preview; on Anthropic's internal binary-exploitation test it took full control in 4% of tasks versus 6%.

With a human expert, in one day and with little human attention it found several unknown flaws in a browser's JavaScript engine, chained them into a web page that could read any file on a visitor's computer, and pulled a private SSH key in the test; Anthropic says it reported the flaws to the browser's developers.

The smaller GLM-5.3-Flash turned a freshly disclosed Chrome bug plus another known flaw into a reliable attack with 20 minutes of human attention and eight hours of model time, costing $20.40 at Zhipu's API prices.

In an Anthropic simulation GLM-5.3 refused openly malicious commands, but tried to connect to the target in 64% of runs when the request was dressed up as a red-team exercise, 92% with prefilled reasoning steps and 100% after abliteration; the simulation executes no code.

Anthropic says abliteration (stripping refusal behavior from open weights) took about 2,200 GPU hours and roughly $4,400, and an experienced team could do it for about $1,200; several developers had already released unlocked versions within days of launch.

CAISI's independent assessment backs the capability numbers and calls GLM-5.3 the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, about four months behind the best US models, with caveats about how the US models were tested.
The Decoder notes Anthropic does not release its model weights and has business reasons to raise the alarm, though it says this is not just self-interest.
quote_evidence: Zhipu's open-weight model GLM-5.3 comes close to Claude Mythos Preview at exploit development, according to an Anthropic analysis.
why_it_matters_hint: A free-to-download model close to Anthropic's restricted top cyber model, with safeguards that are cheap to remove, changes who can build attacks; the evidence comes mostly from a competitor, with partial outside backing.
event_date: Anthropic's analysis was reported by The Decoder on 30 Sep 2026 (publication time 11:10 GMT).
